argument: Prompt-based interventions (safe suffixes, input template alterations) can partially improve safety in post-trained reasoning LLMs but are insufficient and introduce a trade-off between safety and reasoning performance.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported LRMs and the specific prompt modifications tested; transfer to other models or prompt strategies is unestablished.
claim: Prompt-based interventions (safe suffixes, input template alterations) can partially improve safety in post-trained reasoning LLMs but are insufficient and introduce a trade-off between safety and reasoning performance.
conditions: The model is a post-trained LRM
Interventions are limited to prompt modifications (no internal model changes)
Evaluation includes both safety and reasoning performance metrics
falsifier: On a post-trained reasoning LLM, apply various safe suffixes or input template alterations and measure both refusal rate on harmful prompts and accuracy on reasoning benchmarks; verify that safety gains are limited and reasoning performance degrades beyond a certain point.
